p:present.title: Verbs now
rule: A verb has one form for everyone: jeg er, du er, vi er.
Most verbs end in -r in the present: snakker, kommer, heter.

p:neg.title: Saying "not"
rule: Put ikke straight after the verb.
Norwegian does not use "do": jeg snakker ikke means "I do not speak".

options: I do not live in Oslo

p:q-yn.title: Yes or no questions
rule: Start with the verb. Then comes the person.
Again, no "do": Snakker du norsk?

p:q-wh.title: Questions with a question word
rule: Question word first, then the verb, then the person.

c:hvordan-går-det.gloss: how are you? (how is it going)

p:gender.title: En, ei, et
rule: Every noun is an en word, an ei word or an et word. All three mean "a".
Learn each noun with its word: en bil, ei bok, et hus.

p:definite.title: Saying "the"
rule: Norwegian puts "the" on the end of the noun.
en words add -en, ei words add -a, et words add -et.

p:modal.title: Can, will, must
rule: After vil, kan and må, the next verb has no ending: jeg kan snakke.
These three never change and never take -r.

p:inf-aa.title: To do something
rule: Å is "to" before a verb: å spise, å snakke.
Use it after verbs like liker and trenger. Do not use it after vil, kan, må.

p:plural.title: More than one
rule: Most nouns add -er: en bil, to biler. Nouns ending in -e add -r: ei jente, to jenter.
Short et words do not change: et hus, to hus.

p:possessive.title: Mine and yours
rule: The owner comes after the noun, and the noun takes "the": bilen min, "my car".
Min and din change with the noun: bilen min, boka mi, huset mitt. Hans and hennes never change.

p:plural-def.title: "The" for more than one
rule: To say "the" for more than one, add -ene: bilene, jentene, husene.
A few common nouns change their vowel: ei bok, bøker, bøkene.

p:v2.title: The verb comes second
rule: The verb is always the second piece of a statement.
If you start with a time or a place, the person moves behind the verb.

p:obj-pron.title: Me, you, him, her
rule: After a verb or a small word like med or til, the person changes form.
jeg > meg, du > deg, han > ham, hun > henne, vi > oss, de > dem.

p:imperative.title: Telling someone to do it
rule: Take the verb and remove the final -e: vente > vent!, komme > kom!
Short verbs stay the same: gå > gå!, se > se!

p:adj-agree.title: Describing words change
rule: A describing word matches its noun: en stor bil, et stort hus, store biler.
Add -t for et words and -e for more than one. The same happens after er: huset er stort.

p:past.title: The past
rule: For the past, most verbs swap -r for -et or -te: snakker > snakket, spiser > spiste.
The form is the same for everyone. Common verbs have their own past form, learned as words.

p:perfect.title: Have done
rule: Har plus a verb form in -et or -t: jeg har snakket, jeg har spist.
Use it as in English, for something that matters now or has no stated time.

examples.no: jeg snakket med ham i går

p:sub.title: Because, that, if
rule: At, fordi and hvis join a second sentence to the first.
After them comes the person, then the verb: fordi jeg er trøtt.

examples.no: jeg sover fordi jeg er trøtt
examples.en: I am sleeping because I am tired
she says that she is coming

quiz.prompt: han tror at det er dyrt
options: he thinks that it is expensive
he knows that it is expensive

p:future.title: Going to
rule: For a plan, use skal plus the verb with no ending: jeg skal reise.
With a time word, the present is enough: jeg reiser i morgen.

examples.en: I am going to travel tomorrow
what are you going to do?

options: we are going to eat out

p:det-subj.title: It rains, it is cold
rule: Weather and general statements start with det, like English "it": det regner.
The describing word takes -t after det: det er kaldt, det er varmt.

lines.no: Se på bordet.
lines.en: Look on the table.

lines.no: Nei, de ligger ikke der.
lines.en: No, they are not there.

lines.no: Har du dem i bilen?
lines.en: Do you have them in the car?

lines.no: Ja! De ligger i bilen. Kom!
lines.en: Yes! They are in the car. Come!

lines.no: Bra. Kan du gi meg nøkkelen? Jeg vil kjøre.
lines.en: Good. Can you give me the key? I want to drive.

lines.no: Jeg trenger ei ny jakke. Denne er for liten.
lines.en: I need a new jacket. This one is too small.

lines.no: Hvilken farge vil du ha?
lines.en: Which colour do you want?

lines.no: Jeg liker blå klær.
lines.en: I like blue clothes.

lines.no: Se, denne jakka er blå. Og fin!
lines.en: Look, this jacket is blue. And nice!

lines.no: Ja, men hva koster denne?
lines.en: Yes, but how much is this one?

lines.no: Jakka er veldig dyr.
lines.en: The jacket is very expensive.

lines.no: Har de en annen butikk i nærheten?
lines.en: Is there another shop nearby?

lines.no: Ja, ved stasjonen. Klærne der er billige.
lines.en: Yes, by the station. The clothes there are cheap.

questions.prompt: Why does Nora need a new jacket?

options: in the shop by the station

lines.no: Dette er broren min. Han er høy, ikke sant?
lines.en: This is my brother. He is tall, isn't he?

lines.no: Ja! Og han ser snill ut.
lines.en: Yes! And he looks kind.

lines.no: Han er snill og veldig morsom.
lines.en: He is kind and very funny.

lines.no: Har han barn?
lines.en: Does he have children?

lines.no: Ja, to små jenter. De er fire og seks år gamle.
lines.en: Yes, two small girls. They are four and six years old.

lines.no: Og huset? Er det huset hans?
lines.en: And the house? Is it his house?

lines.no: Nei, det er huset vårt i Italia. Det er gammelt, men fint.
lines.en: No, it is our house in Italy. It is old, but nice.

questions.prompt: How many children does the brother have?

lines.no: Hva gjorde du i helga?
lines.en: What did you do at the weekend?

lines.no: Vi dro til fjellet. Vi gikk en lang tur.
lines.en: We went to the mountains. We went for a long walk.

lines.no: Var været fint?
lines.en: Was the weather nice?

lines.no: Nei, det var kaldt. Men vi hadde det gøy.
lines.en: No, it was cold. But we had fun.

lines.no: Hvor bodde dere?
lines.en: Where did you stay?

lines.no: Vi bodde på et lite hotell ved sjøen.
lines.en: We stayed at a small hotel by the lake.

lines.no: Jeg var hjemme. Jeg leste og sov.
lines.en: I was at home. I read and slept.

lines.no: Det er også fint!
lines.en: That is nice too!

options: in a small hotel by the lake

lines.no: I går kom jeg sent hjem. Og jeg hadde ikke nøkkelen!
lines.en: Yesterday I came home late. And I did not have the key!

lines.no: Hva gjorde du da?
lines.en: What did you do then?

lines.no: Jeg satt foran døra og ventet.
lines.en: I sat in front of the door and waited.

lines.no: Kom kona di hjem?
lines.en: Did your wife come home?

lines.no: Ja, klokka ti. Hun så meg og sa: Hva gjør du her?
lines.en: Yes, at ten o'clock. She saw me and said: What are you doing here?

lines.no: Og hva svarte du?
lines.en: And what did you answer?

lines.no: Jeg sa: Jeg glemte nøkkelen på jobb.
lines.en: I said: I forgot the key at work.

questions.prompt: When did Per's wife come home?

lines.no: Hei. Hvorfor har du kommet i dag?
lines.en: Hi. Why have you come today?

lines.no: Jeg føler meg dårlig. Jeg har vondt i hodet.
lines.en: I feel unwell. I have a headache.

lines.no: Har du spist i dag?
lines.en: Have you eaten today?

lines.no: Nei, jeg har ikke spist ennå. Jeg er ikke sulten.
lines.en: No, I have not eaten yet. I am not hungry.

lines.no: Jobber du?
lines.en: Do you work?

lines.no: Ja, jeg har jobbet veldig lenge hver dag. Sjefen sier at det er viktig.
lines.en: Yes, I have worked very long every day. The boss says that it is important.

lines.no: Jeg tror at du er trøtt. Du må bli hjemme og sove.
lines.en: I think that you are tired. You must stay at home and sleep.

lines.no: Heldigvis har jeg fri i morgen.
lines.en: Luckily I am off work tomorrow.

questions.prompt: What does the doctor tell Tom to do?

lines.no: Hei, jeg er ny her. Er denne stolen ledig?
lines.en: Hi, I am new here. Is this chair free?

lines.no: Ja, selvfølgelig. Har du møtt sjefen ennå?
lines.en: Yes, of course. Have you met the boss yet?

lines.no: Nei, hun er opptatt. Jeg prøver igjen snart.
lines.en: No, she is busy. I will try again soon.

lines.no: Hvorfor har du kommet til Norge?
lines.en: Why have you come to Norway?

lines.no: Fordi kjæresten min bor her. Og jeg synes at Norge er et fint land.
lines.en: Because my boyfriend lives here. And I think that Norway is a nice country.

lines.no: Du snakker bra norsk! Hvor har du lært språket?
lines.en: You speak good Norwegian! Where have you learned the language?

lines.no: Jeg har studert norsk i Italia. Men jeg har ikke brukt språket ofte.
lines.en: I have studied Norwegian in Italy. But I have not used the language often.

questions.prompt: Why did Maria come to Norway?

lines.no: Hva skal du gjøre i helga?
lines.en: What are you going to do at the weekend?

lines.no: Jeg vet ikke ennå. Og du?
lines.en: I do not know yet. And you?

lines.no: Det skal snø, og jeg har lyst til å gå på ski. Vil du komme?
lines.en: It is going to snow, and I feel like going skiing. Do you want to come?

lines.no: Det høres bra ut! Men jeg har ikke ski.
lines.en: That sounds good! But I do not have skis.

lines.no: Broren min har ski. Du kan bruke dem.
lines.en: My brother has skis. You can use them.

lines.no: Tusen takk. Når skal vi dra?
lines.en: Thank you very much. When are we going to leave?

lines.no: Tidlig på lørdag. Vi ses klokka åtte!
lines.en: Early on Saturday. See you at eight o'clock!

questions.prompt: What are they going to do?

lines.no: Jonas har bursdag neste uke. Skal vi kjøpe en gave?
lines.en: It is Jonas's birthday next week. Shall we buy a present?

lines.no: Ja. Hva liker han?
lines.en: Yes. What does he like?

lines.no: Han liker film og fotball.
lines.en: He likes film and football.

lines.no: Vi kan gi ham to billetter til kino.
lines.en: We can give him two tickets to the cinema.

lines.no: Det er en god gave! Skal han ha fest?
lines.en: That is a good present! Is he going to have a party?

lines.no: Ja, på fredag. Jeg gleder meg til festen.
lines.en: Yes, on Friday. I am looking forward to the party.

lines.no: Jeg kan dessverre ikke komme på fredag. Jeg skal jobbe.
lines.en: Unfortunately I cannot come on Friday. I am going to work.
